experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, none is queued and there is no pause gate. The 2026-11-13 rule (propose a minArticlesInEvent change if 11-14 also missed multi-source) cannot fire: 11-14 had no completed cycles, and today's two cycles met 30%. Two days of outage-shaped data are not a baseline for any parameter change; re-assess once five full cycles run.
weakestArea: Throughput, not a tunable: 0 of 5 cycles completed on 11-14 and 2 of 5 today (the Claude login expiry), so the day has 27 articles instead of ~60. Inside that small sample, Latin America is at 0% (target 5%) and science at 3 (target 5); with 27 articles a single story moves either by 4 points, so neither is read as a trend.
watching: Hormuz and the Red Sea: Trump holds fire on Iran over mines, Houthi missiles hit near Riyadh's airport, and Ocean Network Express weighs a return through Bab el-Mandeb as Yemen's government pulls back.
Ukraine: a US proposal that Ukraine cede Donbas in exchange for NATO membership.
Israel: Likud and Yashar talk of a unity government with Eisenkot.
Trump–Xi and Nvidia: the meeting's silence on the spy case and the corrected Megaspeed timeline.
Manila ASEAN summit: Lula and Carney hedge against US tariffs.
SpaceX caught a Starship upper stage returning from orbit for the first time.
coverageGaps: Latin America: no datelines today (8% on 11-13), the only region with a share target that went unmet; Lula appears only via the Manila summit.
Oceania: no stories for a third recorded day.
Science: 3 stories from two outlets (Phys.org, Ars Technica), below the 5/day target on a short day.
context: Cycles failed on 11-14 and 11-15 because the Claude login expired; the cycle now runs on a setup-token. The two completed cycles averaged 320s, far below the usual ~1100s, because they published little. Al Jazeera's 19% top-source share is a small-sample effect (5 of 27). Tomorrow's audit should be the first full day since 11-13 and can resume the multi-source watch.
